title: Estar + gerund: what is happening right now
summary: Estoy comiendo, están leyendo: the -ando / -iendo form for actions in progress.
focus: Forming the gerund; estar + gerund vs the simple present
content:
## Forming the gerund

| infinitive | gerund | |
|---|---|---|
| -ar: hablar | habl**ando** | speaking |
| -er: comer | com**iendo** | eating |
| -ir: vivir | viv**iendo** | living |

Spelling: when the stem ends in a vowel, **-iendo** becomes **-yendo**: *leer → leyendo*, *oír → oyendo*, *ir → yendo*. A few -ir verbs change the stem: *dormir → durmiendo*, *decir → diciendo*, *pedir → pidiendo*.

The gerund never changes for person or number.

## Estar + gerund

For an action **in progress right now**, use the present of *estar* + gerund:

- *Estoy comiendo.*: I'm eating (right now).
- *¿Qué estás haciendo?*: What are you doing?
- *Los niños están durmiendo.*: The children are sleeping.
- *Estamos aprendiendo español.*: We're learning Spanish.

Reflexive pronouns go before *estar* or on the gerund: *Me estoy duchando* = *Estoy duchándome* (note the accent).

## Simple present or progressive?

Spanish uses the **simple present** far more than English uses it. *Como a las dos* can mean *I eat at two* or *I'm eating at two*. Use the progressive to stress that something is happening **at this moment**:

- *Trabajo en un banco.*: I work in a bank. (in general)
- *Estoy trabajando.*: I'm working. (right now, don't interrupt)

Never use the progressive for the future: *Mañana trabajo* or *Mañana voy a trabajar*, not *estoy trabajando mañana*.

quiz.explanation: Stem ends in a vowel: -iendo becomes -yendo.
The progressive uses estar: estás haciendo.

quiz.prompt: Translate: We are learning Spanish (right now).
Which is the normal way to say 'I work in a bank' (in general)?
quiz.explanation: Habits and general facts use the simple present.
The progressive is not used for the future; use the simple present or ir a.
The pronoun attaches to the gerund, with an accent added.

listening.note: Leer becomes leyendo: -iendo after a vowel is -yendo.

listening.text: Ahora mismo estoy esperando el autobús.
listening.meaning: Right now I'm waiting for the bus.

listening.text: Estoy leyendo el periódico en la cama.
listening.meaning: I'm reading the newspaper in bed.
listening.note: New word: el periódico = the newspaper.

listening.text: En este momento no puedo hablar, estoy trabajando.
listening.meaning: I can't talk at the moment, I'm working.

listening.text: Mi hermana está hablando por teléfono con una amiga.
listening.meaning: My sister is talking on the phone with a friend.

listening.text: Los niños ya están durmiendo y mi padre todavía está trabajando.
listening.meaning: The children are already asleep and my father is still working.

bites.title: Live action = estar + -ndo
bites.rule: For something happening this very second, use estar + gerund: estoy comiendo. Only estar changes for the person; the gerund never changes.

bites.title: -ando or -iendo
bites.rule: -ar verbs take -ando (hablando); -er and -ir verbs share -iendo (comiendo, viviendo).

bites.title: Vowel before -iendo: y
bites.rule: When the stem ends in a vowel, -iendo becomes -yendo: leyendo, oyendo, yendo. A few -ir verbs also change their stem: durmiendo, pidiendo, diciendo.

bites.title: Don't overuse it
bites.rule: Spanish keeps the simple present for habits and the future: trabajo en un banco, mañana trabajo. Save estar + -ndo for right now.
bites.example: Hoy no trabaja. Está hablando por teléfono.
bites.example_meaning: She's not working today. She's on the phone.

sorts.title: -ando, -iendo or -yendo?
sorts.why: -ar verbs take -ando, -er/-ir take -iendo, and a stem ending in a vowel turns -iendo into -yendo.

sorts.title: Simple present or progressive?

items.text: I work in a bank (in general)
I'm eating right now, call later
The kids are sleeping at the moment
I eat at two every day
She's talking on the phone right now

sorts.why: Use estar + gerund only for what is in progress right now; habits and future plans take the simple present.

sorts.title: Stem change in the gerund?
sorts.why: A few -ir verbs shift o → u or e → i in the gerund; most verbs keep their stem.

spots.why: The progressive always uses estar: están durmiendo.
Leer's stem ends in a vowel, so -iendo becomes -yendo.
Dormir changes o → u in the gerund: durmiendo.
Estar needs a gerund, not an infinitive: aprendiendo.
The verb estar carries an accent: está.

builds.text: Está hablando por teléfono con la abuela.
builds.meaning: She's talking to Grandma on the phone.
